findings.evidence: scripts/check-drift.sh:76 THRESHOLD_RE='...|_ms|_seconds' against its own header at :59-62. Measured in a scratch repo: a file containing `let err_msg = std::env::var("OQUEUE_BANNER").unwrap_or_default();` produces 'FAIL threshold made settable'. There is no suppression mechanism anywhere in the script, so the only exits are renaming a legitimate variable or widening a non-negotiable-2 gate's regex. dfd1406's body records the fix (`_ms([^a-z0-9]|$)`).
findings.summary: check-drift.sh's new _ms alternative matches _msg as a substring, so a legitimate env::var line fails non-negotiable 2's gate with a remedy that misdiagnoses it, and the header's promised 'cheap to dismiss on sight' escape does not exist.

findings.evidence: scripts/gates/m0-complete.sh:352 versus scripts/lib.sh:14 `set -euo pipefail`. Trigger: writing `readonly THRESHOLD_RE=` or indenting the assignment in check-drift.sh. Compare m0-complete.sh:423-428 ('fail and carry on, never finish') and backlog.md:743-744. Sections 6, 7 and 8 - including the boundary-review refusal - never run.
findings.summary: m0-complete.sh's THRESHOLD_RE extraction has no || true, so under lib.sh's set -euo pipefail a non-matching grep aborts the whole gate and the fail branch two lines below is unreachable - the early-abort shape M0.26 removed from section 5b in the very next commit.
